market_brief: The AI trade cracked again on Tuesday: the SOX fell 7.9% and the Nasdaq 100 2.0% as Nvidia gave back part of its Huang-return surge, while rotation into value and retail lifted the Dow 0.9% to a first close above 50,000 and the equal-weight S&P rose 0.5%. The selloff is spreading through Asia this morning, with Kospi down about 4.5% and Nikkei 2.4%, as Indian markets reopen after Monday's 1.75% Nifty drop. Strong US consumer confidence (103.3) keeps a Dec 9 Fed hike near-certain, though the 10Y eased to 4.90% and DXY slipped 0.5% to 103.8. Metals extended their rout (gold -2.6% to $3,555, silver -5.6%), bitcoin hovers just under $60k, and US natural gas jumped 15% on cold weather; today's PCE and GDP are the key catalysts before Thanksgiving.
ai_brief: Compute deals dominate: Anthropic is reportedly close to a ~$45bn Nscale capacity deal and, per the NYT, pays about $3.1bn a month for Musk-controlled compute. Product news was incremental, including Perplexity Teammates, wider Gemini 4 access in Antigravity and a unified Claude Plugins directory, while Nvidia's Vera Rubin topped a provisional MLPerf agentic round. LeCun's attack on Anthropic's safety messaging is the most-discussed post.

items.headline: Chips give back Monday's surge: SOX falls 7.9% while the Dow closes above 50,000 for the first time
items.summary: Every SOX member closed lower as Nvidia fell 5.9% to $155.38 (about $240bn of value), AMD 8.9% and Micron about 11%, a day after Nvidia's 31% jump on Huang's return. Money rotated into value and retail names: the Dow gained 423 points to 50,018.70 while the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.5% and the S&P 500 0.5%.

items.headline: Kospi sinks about 4.5% and Nikkei 2.4% in early Wednesday trade as the chip selloff spreads to Asia
items.summary: Kospi fell back below 5,000 to around 4,783 by mid-morning Seoul time and the Nikkei traded near 57,265. Samsung and SK Hynix dropped more than 6%, Kioxia about 12% and SoftBank Group almost 10%, per early-session reports.

items.headline: Dell posts record $54.9bn quarter, guides FY27 revenue to $202bn and adds $25bn to its buyback
items.summary: Revenue roughly doubled year on year with adjusted EPS of $9.45 against about $6.56 expected; AI orders were $60.2bn and backlog reached $132.3bn. Shares rose about 4% after hours after falling roughly 12% in the regular session; AI-server mix squeezed gross margins.

items.headline: Workday and Autodesk slip after hours despite beats and raised full-year outlooks
items.summary: Autodesk beat on revenue ($2.16bn, +17%) and EPS ($3.20) and lifted FY27 guidance but fell 4-5% as free-cash-flow margin narrowed. Workday raised FY27 subscription guidance to $9.96bn, yet its Q4 subscription outlook implied a slowdown to about 10% growth and shares fell 4-8%.

items.headline: After-hours: Ambarella plunges about 39% on memory-cost warning; Nutanix CEO to step down
items.summary: Ambarella guided Q4 revenue to $70-75m from $115m, saying rising memory prices are making customers cut forecasts. Nutanix fell about 8% as CEO Rajiv Ramaswami said he will leave once a successor is found; Urban Outfitters dropped about 12% on in-line sales while GoodRx rose about 18%.

items.headline: HP Inc. beats, guides FY27 EPS above consensus and raises its dividend
items.summary: Fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS of $0.83 and revenue of $16.0bn topped estimates; FY27 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.15-3.45 brackets a midpoint above the Street's $3.18. The quarterly dividend rises to $0.31; reports differ on the size of the after-hours gain.

items.headline: Update: AI-supply-chain beats get punished: Analog Devices has its worst day since 1998
items.summary: Analog Devices closed down about 17% despite 42% revenue growth, with HPE (-16%), Semtech (-17%) and Dycom (-18%) also sliding after strong reports. Earlier coverage flagged premarket weakness; the closes show the selling deepened through the session.

items.headline: Retailers rally on beat-and-raise quarters: Kohl's and Abercrombie up about 20%
items.summary: Kohl's raised its outlook and Abercrombie posted record Q3 sales with higher EPS guidance; Dick's (+15%), Dollar Tree (+11%) and Best Buy (+3%) also lifted forecasts. The moves underpinned the day's rotation out of chips into consumer and value stocks.

items.headline: US consumer confidence jumps to 103.3, highest since January 2025 and far above forecasts
items.summary: The Conference Board index rose from an upwardly revised 91.9, against a 92.5 consensus. One economist linked the rebound to reduced uncertainty after the midterm elections; the strength adds to the case for a December Fed hike.

items.headline: Fed futures hold about 95% odds of a 25bp hike on Dec 9 as January odds climb to 69%
items.summary: CME FedWatch shows a 50bp move priced out after Monday's rally, while odds of a further hike in January rose from 49% on Nov 20 to 69% and June to about 62%. October PCE due Wednesday is the next test before the Dec 4 jobs report.

items.headline: Oil rebounds from three-month lows on fresh Hormuz attacks; strait traffic down more than 40%
items.summary: Brent touched about $88 (lowest since late August) before rising more than $1 after Iran said tankers hit mines; Deutsche Bank estimates an oversupply of about 1.7m bpd. MarineTraffic data cited by Al Jazeera show weekly Hormuz crossings fell from 226 to 125 over November.

items.headline: Indian markets reopen after the holiday into a weak Asian tape; Nifty supports seen at 25,000-25,300
items.summary: Nifty last closed Monday at 25,349.65 (-1.75%) and Bank Nifty fell 3.2%; brokers flag resistance near 25,500-25,650 and advise caution on fresh longs. FIIs have reportedly bought about Rs 1.21 lakh crore of equities in November, led by financials.

items.headline: Update: Huang and Nvidia's general counsel set to testify to the House on Dec 1 and Senate Banking on Dec 3
items.summary: Congressional scrutiny of the reinstatement is widening, with a California DOJ probe also reported ongoing. Huang reportedly used his first day back to apologise to staff at an all-hands meeting.

items.headline: Hacker News and fintwit debate a Foreign Policy op-ed calling Huang's return a national-security scandal
items.summary: The op-ed drew one of the week's busiest discussion threads, per a digest of trending posts. Commentary focuses on whether political involvement in the reinstatement creates export-control risk for Nvidia holders.

items.headline: Today: US October PCE and Q3 GDP; US markets shut Thursday for Thanksgiving, Bank of Korea decides
items.summary: PCE and GDP land on Wednesday ahead of a holiday-shortened week, with the Bank of Korea widely expected to hike on Thursday. Next week brings Huang's Dec 1 and Dec 3 testimony, then the Dec 4 jobs report and the Dec 8-9 FOMC.

items.headline: Nscale reportedly nears a second Anthropic deal worth about $45bn for 460MW in West Virginia
items.summary: The capacity at Nscale's Monarch campus would run on Nvidia Vera Rubin chips, per the report; neither company has confirmed terms.

items.headline: Update: NYT reports Anthropic pays about $3.1bn a month for Musk-controlled compute; Google about $800m
items.summary: Adds figures to earlier reports that xAI is pivoting toward renting out compute, with Anthropic its largest customer. The arrangement makes SpaceX a supplier to two of xAI's direct rivals.

items.headline: Perplexity launches Teammates, personal work agents that can take on several roles
items.summary: Teammates operate inside a shared workspace and are available to $200-a-month Max subscribers first, per launch coverage.

items.headline: Gemini 4 Carbon comes to AI Pro subscribers in Antigravity; Cursor adds Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: Carbon was previously limited to AI Ultra in Google's agentic IDE. Separately, Cursor reportedly measured Gemini 4 Neon at 63.7% on CursorBench versus 57.3% for Gemini 4 Hydrogen.

items.headline: Gemini API adds file-slicing controls and native Office/OpenDocument uploads
items.summary: Developers can load only selected PDF pages, spreadsheet cells or media segments, cutting token use on large files.

items.headline: Claude merges connectors and skills into a single Plugins directory with 10,000+ options
items.summary: The page is live on Free, Pro, Max and Ultra plans, with Team and Enterprise to follow, per reports.

items.headline: Vera Rubin NVL72 leads MLPerf's first agentic-inference Endpoints round (provisional)
items.summary: Nvidia claims 5-10x throughput per kilowatt over GB300; results are still pending MLCommons peer review.

items.headline: Microsoft begins validating its first AMD Helios rack in an Azure research lab
items.summary: Helios combines MI455X GPUs with EPYC CPUs and Pensando networking, a step toward rack-scale competition with Nvidia.

items.headline: Applied Digital signs an 18-year, $5.4bn, 150MW data-centre lease with an unnamed hyperscaler
items.summary: The deal extends the run of long-dated AI capacity contracts even as AI-linked equities sell off.

items.headline: LeCun says on X that Amodei is hyping AI dangers to get open-source models outlawed
items.summary: The post sparked a 1,400-point Hacker News thread, reigniting the open-weights versus safety-regulation debate.

items.headline: Trending: skill-distill turns Claude Code or Codex sessions into skills open-weight models can follow
items.summary: The Python repo gathered about 530 stars in a week; most other top trending repos were game-emulation projects.

items.headline: What AI newsletters are focused on: Nvidia's leadership saga, PR-review agents and GPT-6.2 Sol
items.summary: Daily digests led with Huang's reinstatement, Claude Ship, OpenAI's chat-tuned GPT-6.2 Sol and Anthropic's unreviewed VP-vs-VNP proof claim.
